issues.description: Class name and file contents mismatch in the template: the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a public class named AnimalFarm and contains duplicated/garbled content (a second 'package' declaration and a duplicated AnimalFarm skeleton). The problem statement and the solution repository expect a public class named Farm (with methods addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong and a private List<Animal> animals). This naming/content mismatch will cause compilation errors (public class name must match the file name) and prevents students from implementing the UML-specified Farm class or running the provided Main.java, blocking progress.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a properly named and structured Farm class that matches the assignment and solution. Specifically: (1) Rename the public class from AnimalFarm to Farm so the class name matches the file Farm.java; (2) remove the duplicated/garbled package declaration and duplicate class fragments; (3) implement the expected private List<Animal> animals field and a no-argument constructor that initializes it to new ArrayList<>(); (4) provide getter/setter for animals, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals() that prints each animal.messageOnFeed(), and singFarmSong() which iterates animals and calls a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal) helper. Keep the file package declaration 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' at the top. This will align the template with the problem statement and solution and avoid compilation/blocking errors for students.
